To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a low-offset high-speed dynamic latched comparator with a complementary output latch stage was proposed and the circuit showed up to 25 % lower input-referred offset and 44% lower sensitivity of the delay to the input voltage difference than the conventional dynamic latch comparator.

a new dynamic latching comparator with two additional inverters and a dual-rail architecture is proposed, which shows up to 44% less delay/log(ΔVin) than the conventional double tail latching comparator at approximately the 50% area and 50% power consumption.
a new dynamic latcher comparator is proposed and its performances are evaluated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new dynamic latcher comparator which shows lower latch offset voltage and faster latch speed than the conventional comparators.

the design and implementation of a new dynamic comparator which shows lower latch offset voltage and better speed characteristics than the conventional dynamic comparator at approximately the similar area and power consumption.
the design of high speed low offset dynamic latched comparator for the application in low-voltage high-speed data conversion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed dynamic latched comparator is a very good candidate for the high-speed applications, where low offset and high load drivability are required.
the proposed dynamic latched comparator is suitable for high-speed applications with low-offset requirements.
the proposed comparator shows better performance in terms of the delay/log(ΔVin) and input-referred latch-offset voltage than the conventional double tail comparator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have improved the conventional dynamic latches in terms of offset voltage and load drive capability by using the complementary output stage, and the dynamic latch comparator in terms of offset and delay sensitivity by using the additional gain stage.
the circuit shows a good performance in terms of the input-referred latch offsets, the delay, and the power consumption.
the circuit shows a better performance than the conventional double tail latched comparator with a small increase in the area and power consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed circuit is a good candidate for the comparator in the high-speed ADC applications.

the proposed circuit can be used for the applications which demand a high-speed operation with a very low input-referred latch-offset voltage, such as the applications where the comparator is used in the pipeline stages of the ADCs.
the dynamic latched comparator with the proposed structure shows a better performance than the conventional dynamic comparator with the same area and the same power consumption.
